source_text: Et uenimus prope locum, cuius loci parietes tales erant quasi de luce aedificati; et ante ostium loci illius angeli quattuor introeuntes uestierunt nos stolas candidas. Et introiuimus, et audiuimus uocem unitam dicentem: Agios, agios, agios, sine cessatione. Et uidimus in eodem loco sedentem quasi hominem canum, niueos habentem capillos et uultu iuuenili, cuius pedes non uidimus. Et in dextera et in sinistra eius seniores quattuor, et post illos ceteri seniores conplures. Introiuimus cum admiratione et stetimus ante thronum, et quattuor angeli subleuauerunt nos, et osculati sumus illum, et de manu sua traiecit nobis in faciem. Et ceteri seniores dixerunt nobis: Stemus ad orationem. Et stetimus et pacem fecimus. Et dixerunt nobis seniores: Ite et ludite. Et dixi Perpetuae: Habes quod uis. Et dixit mihi: Deo gratias, ut, quomodo in carne hilaris fui, hilarior sim et hic modo.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: and we came up close to a place, and the walls of that place were as though constructed out of light; and in front of the door of that place four angels, as we were going in, put white robes on us. And we entered, and we heard a joined voice saying Holy, holy, holy unceasingly. And we saw seated in the same place one like a grey-haired man, having snow-like hair and a youthful countenance, whose feet we did not see. And on his right and on his left four elders, and behind them a great many remaining elders. We went in with amazement and stood before the throne, and the four angels raised us up, and we kissed him, and from his hand he drew across over our face. And the remaining elders said to us Let us stand for prayer. And we stood and made the peace. And the elders said to us Go and play. And I said to Perpetua You have what you want. And she said to me Thanks to God, that just as I was cheerful in flesh, so now I am more cheerful here.
pass_b_english: We came near to the place whose walls were as if built of light, and before the door of that place four angels, as we entered, clothed us in white robes. And we went in, and we heard a united voice saying, "Holy, holy, holy," without ceasing (Isa 6:3; Rev 4:8). And in that same place we saw one seated like an aged man, white-haired, with snow-white hair and a youthful face, whose feet we did not see. And at his right and at his left were four elders, and behind them many other elders.

We entered in wonder and stood before the throne, and the four angels lifted us up, and we kissed him, and from his hand he drew across our faces. And the other elders said to us, "Let us stand for prayer." And we stood and exchanged the peace. And the elders said to us, "Go and play." And I said to Perpetua, "You have what you wish." And she said to me, "Thanks be to God, that as I was joyful in the flesh, I am more joyful here now."

choices.term: quasi hominem canum, niueos habentem capillos et uultu iuuenili
choices.english: like an aged man, white-haired, with snow-white hair and a youthful face
choices.why: canum marks aged greyness while niueos capillos repeats whiteness literally and uultu iuuenili is ablative of description, so the contrast of age and youth is kept rather than smoothing it
rejected: like an old man with white hair and a young face

choices.why: ludite is second plural imperative of ludo in a festal heavenly court context, so play or sport fits the joy motif rather than a moral command

choices.term: de manu sua traiecit nobis in faciem
choices.english: from his hand he drew across our faces
choices.why: traiecit with in faciem describes a stroking or tracing gesture from the hand toward the face, not giving an object, so a vague drawing-across rendering stays closer than supplying a sign of the cross
rejected: he made the sign of the cross on our faces
